references.text: A previous command in the same chapter that Passover shall be a permanent ordinance for the people of Israel through all generations.
Reiterates the command to observe this statute at the appointed time year after year, as a lasting ordinance.
Moses reiterates the Passover regulations to the people and emphasizes that they are to be kept as an eternal ordinance.
Command to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread as a permanent statute throughout all generations.
This night shall be observed for the Lord by all the children of Israel through all their generations.
The command to tell your children about the exodus from Egypt and that it shall be a sign for future generations.
The Israelites celebrate Passover at Gilgal after entering the promised land, fulfilling the eternal statute.
King Hezekiah restores the celebration of Passover in Israel as a confirmation of the eternal ordinance given to the fathers.
The Jews who returned from exile celebrated Passover, thus continuing the eternal ordinance.
A theological connection between the transmission of the statute and the blessing that follows for coming generations.
A strong thematic parallel regarding the passing on of God's commands to the next generation as a basis for blessing.
Specifying 'your children' to include multiple generations to emphasize the permanence of the covenant.
